info.title: Biohub scorer (from official patched metric)
info.subtitle: Official competition metric + scripts, for offline kernels
info.description:
An **unmodified copy of the official Biohub cell-tracking competition code**
(`royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition`), packaged as a Kaggle dataset so that
**no-internet kernels** can import it. All credit to the competition organisers; this
is a redistribution for convenience, not original work.

## Why you might want this

Competition kernels run without internet, so you cannot `pip install` or `git clone`
the official package. Attaching this dataset lets you:

- **Score a submission offline with the official metric before spending a daily
  submission slot** - the repo ships `scripts/csv_to_geffs.py` and
  `scripts/evaluate.py`, which together implement the round trip the organisers
  document: predict -> geffs -> CSV -> geffs -> score. No images are loaded.
- Read the exact metric implementation rather than a paraphrase of it.
- Reuse the official training and prediction scripts.

## Important: this is the PATCHED metric

Pinned at commit `075fc5f5a52d11077f9dc2b074644618f26939e2`, which includes
`aa65e90` *"updating metric to patch weakly connected component exploit"*
(2026-07-17).

Some widely used support packs vendor an **older copy** of this code that predates
that patch and still contains `_weakly_connected_components`. If you score locally
with one of those, your division numbers are computed with the pre-patch metric.
A one-line check:

```python
import inspect, tracking_cellmot.division_metrics as dm
assert "_weakly_connected_components" not in inspect.getsource(dm)
```

For reference, the patch changed `division_metrics.py` from 450 to 574 lines
(division scoring substantially rewritten) and 90 lines of `metrics.py`. The
edge-side changes - non-consecutive-edge filtering and duplicate-edge dedup - are
no-ops for graphs that already use consecutive-frame edges with in-degree 1, so if
that describes your output, only your **division** numbers change.

## Caveat on local scoring

Train labels are sparse: annotated edges cover a small fraction of cells, and the
metric ignores edges whose endpoints match no annotated node. A local score is a
useful diagnostic and a good way to catch invalid graphs, but it is **not** a
reliable predictor of leaderboard rank - in our own testing the local ranking of
two pipelines came out inverted relative to the public leaderboard. Treat it
accordingly.

## Contents

- `tracking_cellmot_075fc5f/src/tracking_cellmot/` - the package (`metrics.py`,
  `division_metrics.py`, `io.py`, `img_proc.py`, `models/`)
- `tracking_cellmot_075fc5f/scripts/` - `evaluate.py`, `csv_to_geffs.py`,
  `geffs_to_csv.py`, `train_unet_transformer.py`, `predict_unet_transformer.py`
- `metrics.md` - the organisers' description of the metric
- `USAGE.md` - copy-paste snippets, including how to verify the patched version
  loaded and the `GraphView.detach()` gotcha
- `PROVENANCE.md`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`
